beats.beat: Rowe and the sexton find the cracked beam, repair costs fifteen pounds against four in the poor box.
Rowe goes to the library above the draper's, Judith is minding the counter.
Judith offers to keep the subscription book and suggests naming parishioners; Rowe calls it parish politics dressed as advice; she withdraws the offer.
Mrs Pike arrives with news of Miss Marchmont's fortnight at the gatehouse.
Mrs Pike declares this the answer to everything and lists what Rowe must wear, ignoring his protest.

turn.note: Mrs Pike's flat refusal to be dissuaded ('you shall have both') commits the parish to a matchmaking scheme Rowe has explicitly rejected, setting up the dinner in chapter two.

trope_note: Enemies of manner and the meddling matchmaker are both live on the page; the chaperone's absence is not yet relevant and rightly withheld.
fixes: Consider trimming the Mrs Yardley/Hollis sentence slightly for ear-parsing, as it stacks two clauses of financial reasoning back to back.
The 'lid that fits the pot' simile is good but is the chapter's one indulgence in figurative flourish; keep future Pike scenes plainer to avoid it becoming a tic.
